description:
FILED s484d (2026-09-14) -- found by implementing `run_multiple_progs`
(#1652), which made t/io/data.t produce its 4 rows for the first time.  3 pass;
this is the 4th.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl; the file's own size is the third number
so the scale is visible):

    my $start = tell(DATA);
    my $line  = <DATA>;
    my $after = tell(DATA);
    print "size=", -s $0, " start=$start after=$after\n";
    __DATA__
    ab
    cd

    perl: size=268 start=262 after=265     <- an offset IN THE FILE
    PCL:  size=268 start=0   after=3       <- an offset inside the SECTION

perl's DATA is an ordinary handle onto the script itself, left positioned just
after the `__DATA__`/`__END__` line, so `tell` answers in the file's
coordinates and `seek(DATA, $n, 0)` reaches any byte of the script.  PCL's
DATA is a handle onto the section's text alone, so both answers are relative
to the section.

THE ROW IT COSTS: t/io/data.t's third record
(https://github.com/Perl/perl5/issues/7207) collects `tell(DATA)` at every
`__DATA__` line and compares the list with the positions found by re-reading
`$0` with an ordinary handle -- the two must agree.  Under PCL they cannot.
Measured: io/data.t is DIFF 3/1 (perl 4/0).

FIX SHAPE: open DATA on the SCRIPT and seek to the end of the terminator line,
instead of on a string of the section.  Two things to check while doing it:
(a) `seek(DATA, 0, 0)` then reading must see the whole script (perl's answer),
which is what the "seek DATA back to the start and read to __END__" idiom in
perl's own t/test.pl relies on; (b) a program whose source came from STDIN or
a string eval has no file to open -- perl answers with the in-memory copy it
kept, so PCL's current behaviour has to remain the fallback for those.

VALUE: 1 row in the companion population, so it is a filler.  It is filed
because the row now EXISTS and needs a cause.
subject: `tell(DATA)` is an offset INSIDE the DATA section; perl's is an offset in the SOURCE FILE (io/data.t's one remaining row)
